substantive_reconstruction.dilation: Put S=sqrt(I−Σ²). Both S and Σ are real diagonal, hence commute; the central block M is Hermitian and M² has diagonal Σ²+S²=I and off-diagonal ΣS−SΣ=0. Therefore M†M=I. The two exterior block-diagonal matrices are unitary, so their product U_A is unitary, with blocks [[A,W S],[S V†,−Σ]]. This proves existence, not efficient gate synthesis.
substantive_reconstruction.conditioning: For a normalized b, U_A|0,b⟩=|0⟩Ab+|1⟩S V†b. Orthogonal ancilla branches give p=||Ab||². Conditioning yields Ab/||Ab|| only if p>0; no normalized output is defined on ker A, and A=0 has no successful input. Since I−A†A is positive semidefinite, p=1 exactly on normalized vectors in K=ker(I−A†A), not only when the entire A is unitary. For example diag(1,1/2) succeeds with certainty on the first basis vector.
substantive_reconstruction.operator_boundary: For A=cI the specified dilation succeeds with probability c², whereas the deterministic identity gives the same normalized output for every input without that branch. This does not implement the unnormalized map cI. No nonunitary A can equal one system-only unitary on all vectors. More generally tr(AρA†)=tr(A†Aρ) equals one for every density matrix precisely when A†A=I: testing pure states and polarization proves the converse. No deterministic generic normalized preparation theorem is inferred.
